passages.text: Like snow in summer and rain at harvest, honor does not befit a fool.
passages.sermon:
A fool is a person who acts without wisdom.
Honor means respect or praise.
Snow does not belong in summer.
Rain does not belong at harvest time.
Honor does not belong to a fool.
passages.original: כַּשֶּׁ֤לֶג׀ בַּקַּ֗יִץ וְכַמָּטָ֥ר בַּקָּצִ֑יר כֵּ֤ן לֹא־ נָאוֶ֖ה לִכְסִ֣יל כָּבֽוֹד׃

passages.text: Like a fluttering sparrow or darting swallow, an undeserved curse does not come to rest.
passages.sermon:
A sparrow flutters.
A swallow darts through the air.
An undeserved curse moves like these birds.
The curse does not settle.
The curse does not come to rest.
passages.original: כַּצִּפּ֣וֹר לָ֭נוּד כַּדְּר֣וֹר לָע֑וּף כֵּ֥ן קִֽלְלַ֥ת חִ֝נָּ֗ם לֹא תָבֹֽא׃

passages.text: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the backs of fools!
passages.sermon: A horse needs a whip.\r\nA donkey needs a bridle.\r\nA fool needs a rod on his back.
passages.original: שׁ֣וֹט לַ֭סּוּס מֶ֣תֶג לַחֲמ֑וֹר וְ֝שֵׁ֗בֶט לְגֵ֣ו כְּסִילִֽים׃

passages.text: Do not answer a fool according to his folly, or you yourself will be like him.
passages.sermon: A fool acts with foolishness.\r\nDo not answer a fool in the same foolish way.\r\nIf you answer like him, you will become like him.
passages.original: אַל־ תַּ֣עַן כְּ֭סִיל כְּאִוַּלְתּ֑וֹ פֶּֽן־ תִּשְׁוֶה־ לּ֥וֹ גַם־ אָֽתָּה׃

passages.text: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he become wise in his own eyes.
passages.sermon:
A fool acts with foolishness.
You must answer a fool in a way that matches his foolishness.
If you do not answer him, he may think he is wise.
He may see himself as wise in his own eyes.
passages.original: עֲנֵ֣ה כְ֭סִיל כְּאִוַּלְתּ֑וֹ פֶּן־ יִהְיֶ֖ה חָכָ֣ם בְּעֵינָֽיו׃

passages.text: Like cutting off one’s own feet or drinking violence is the sending of a message by the hand of a fool.
passages.sermon:
A fool is a person who lacks wisdom.
A person sends a message by the hand of a fool.
This action is like cutting off one’s own feet.
This action is also like drinking violence.
Sending a message by a fool brings harm to the sender.
passages.original: מְקַצֶּ֣ה רַ֭גְלַיִם חָמָ֣ס שֹׁתֶ֑ה שֹׁלֵ֖חַ דְּבָרִ֣ים בְּיַד־ כְּסִֽיל׃

passages.text: Like lame legs hanging limp is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
passages.sermon:
A fool speaks proverbs.
A fool does not understand wisdom.
A proverb in a fool’s mouth is useless.
Lame legs hang limp and cannot walk.
A proverb in a fool’s mouth is like lame legs.
It cannot help or guide anyone.
passages.original: דַּלְי֣וּ שֹׁ֭קַיִם מִפִּסֵּ֑חַ וּ֝מָשָׁ֗ל בְּפִ֣י כְסִילִֽים׃

passages.text: Like binding a stone into a sling is the giving of honor to a fool.
passages.sermon:
A fool is a person who lacks wisdom and understanding.
Giving honor to a fool is like binding a stone tightly into a sling.
A stone bound in a sling cannot be thrown.
Honor given to a fool is useless and dangerous.
passages.original: כִּצְר֣וֹר אֶ֭בֶן בְּמַרְגֵּמָ֑ה כֵּן־ נוֹתֵ֖ן לִכְסִ֣יל כָּבֽוֹד׃

passages.text: Like a thorn that falls into the hand of a drunkard is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
passages.sermon:
A fool speaks proverbs.
A fool does not understand wisdom.
A proverb in a fool’s mouth is dangerous.
A drunkard holds a thorn in his hand.
The thorn hurts the drunkard.
A proverb in a fool’s mouth is like a thorn in a drunkard’s hand.
The fool’s words can cause harm.
The fool cannot use wisdom rightly.
The fool’s proverb brings pain, not help.
passages.original: ח֭וֹחַ עָלָ֣ה בְיַד־ שִׁכּ֑וֹר וּ֝מָשָׁ֗ל בְּפִ֣י כְסִילִֽים׃

passages.text: Like an archer who wounds at random is he who hires a fool or passerby.
passages.sermon:
An archer shoots arrows.
He does not aim.
He wounds people at random.
A person hires a fool.
A person hires a passerby.
This is like the archer who wounds at random.
Hiring a fool or a passerby brings harm without purpose.
passages.original: רַ֥ב מְחֽוֹלֵֽל־ כֹּ֑ל וְשֹׂכֵ֥ר כְּ֝סִ֗יל וְשֹׂכֵ֥ר עֹבְרִֽים׃

passages.text: As a dog returns to its vomit, so a fool repeats his folly.
passages.sermon: A dog returns to its vomit.\r\nA fool repeats his foolishness.\r\nA fool does the same wrong things again and again.
passages.original: כְּ֭כֶלֶב שָׁ֣ב עַל־ קֵא֑וֹ כְּ֝סִ֗יל שׁוֹנֶ֥ה בְאִוַּלְתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Do you see a man who is wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
passages.sermon:
A man may think he is wise.
He trusts his own judgment.
He believes he knows what is right.
This man is wise in his own eyes.
A fool often makes mistakes.
Yet there is more hope for the fool than for the proud man.
The man who is wise in his own eyes has less hope than a fool.
passages.original: רָאִ֗יתָ אִ֭ישׁ חָכָ֣ם בְּעֵינָ֑יו תִּקְוָ֖ה לִכְסִ֣יל מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: The slacker says, “A lion is in the road! A fierce lion roams the public square!”
passages.sermon:
A slacker avoids work.
He makes excuses.
He says, “A lion is in the road.”
He says, “A fierce lion is in the public square.”
passages.original: אָמַ֣ר עָ֭צֵל שַׁ֣חַל בַּדָּ֑רֶךְ אֲ֝רִ֗י בֵּ֣ין הָרְחֹבֽוֹת׃

passages.text: As a door turns on its hinges, so the slacker turns on his bed.
passages.sermon:
A slacker is a lazy person.
A door turns on its hinges.
A slacker turns on his bed in the same way.
He does not get up.
He stays in bed and moves around.
He does not take action.
passages.original: הַ֭דֶּלֶת תִּסּ֣וֹב עַל־ צִירָ֑הּ וְ֝עָצֵ֗ל עַל־ מִטָּתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The slacker buries his hand in the dish; it wearies him to bring it back to his mouth.
passages.sermon:
A slacker is a lazy person.
He puts his hand into the dish.
He feels tired.
He does not want to bring his hand back to his mouth.
passages.original: טָ֘מַ֤ן עָצֵ֣ל יָ֭דוֹ בַּצַּלָּ֑חַת נִ֝לְאָ֗ה לַֽהֲשִׁיבָ֥הּ אֶל־ פִּֽיו׃

passages.text: The slacker is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer discreetly.
passages.sermon:
A slacker is a lazy person.
He thinks he is wise.
He believes he knows more than others.
Seven men can answer with good sense.
The slacker still thinks he is wiser than all of them.
passages.original: חָכָ֣ם עָצֵ֣ל בְּעֵינָ֑יו מִ֝שִּׁבְעָ֗ה מְשִׁ֣יבֵי טָֽעַם׃

passages.text: Like one who grabs a dog by the ears is a passerby who meddles in a quarrel not his own.
passages.sermon: A person who grabs a dog by its ears acts recklessly.\r\nA passerby who interferes in a quarrel that does not belong to him acts the same way.\r\nBoth put themselves in danger by meddling in matters that are not theirs.
passages.original: מַחֲזִ֥יק בְּאָזְנֵי־ כָ֑לֶב עֹבֵ֥ר מִ֝תְעַבֵּ֗ר עַל־ רִ֥יב לֹּֽא־ לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Like a madman shooting firebrands and deadly arrows, so is the man who deceives his neighbor and says, “I was only joking!”
passages.sermon:
A madman acts without control.
He shoots firebrands.
He shoots deadly arrows.
He causes danger and harm.
A man who deceives his neighbor acts the same way.
He lies to his friend.
He says, “I was only joking!”
He tries to excuse his deception as a joke.
He causes harm with his words and actions.
He does not take responsibility for the hurt he causes.
passages.original: כְּֽ֭מִתְלַהְלֵהַּ הַיֹּרֶ֥ה זִקִּ֗ים חִצִּ֥ים וָמָֽוֶת׃ כֵּֽן־ אִ֭ישׁ רִמָּ֣ה אֶת־ רֵעֵ֑הוּ וְ֝אָמַ֗ר הֲ‍ֽלֹא־ מְשַׂחֵ֥ק אָֽנִי׃

passages.text: Without wood, a fire goes out; without gossip, a conflict ceases.
passages.sermon:
A fire needs wood to keep burning.
If there is no wood, the fire will go out.
Gossip causes conflict.
If there is no gossip, conflict will stop.
passages.original: בְּאֶ֣פֶס עֵ֭צִים תִּכְבֶּה־ אֵ֑שׁ וּבְאֵ֥ין נִ֝רְגָּ֗ן יִשְׁתֹּ֥ק מָדֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Like charcoal for embers and wood for fire, so is a quarrelsome man for kindling strife.
passages.sermon:
A quarrelsome man starts arguments.
Charcoal makes embers burn.
Wood makes fire grow.
A quarrelsome man makes strife increase.
He causes conflict, just as fuel feeds a fire.
passages.original: פֶּחָ֣ם לְ֭גֶחָלִים וְעֵצִ֣ים לְאֵ֑שׁ וְאִ֥ישׁ מְדוֹנִים לְחַרְחַר־ רִֽיב׃פ

passages.text: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels that go down into the inmost being.
passages.sermon:
A gossip speaks words.
These words seem pleasant.
These words are like tasty food.
These words go deep inside a person.
These words reach the deepest parts of a person’s heart.
passages.original: דִּבְרֵ֣י נִ֭רְגָּן כְּמִֽתְלַהֲמִ֑ים וְ֝הֵ֗ם יָרְד֥וּ חַדְרֵי־ בָֽטֶן׃

passages.text: Like glaze covering an earthen vessel are burning lips and a wicked heart.
passages.sermon:
A person may have burning lips.
This person may speak with passion or intensity.
This person may also have a wicked heart.
A wicked heart means the person has evil intentions inside.
Glaze can cover an earthen vessel.
The glaze hides what is underneath.
In the same way, burning lips can cover a wicked heart.
The outside may look good or attractive.
But the inside is still evil.
passages.original: כֶּ֣סֶף סִ֭יגִים מְצֻפֶּ֣ה עַל־ חָ֑רֶשׂ שְׂפָתַ֖יִם דֹּלְקִ֣ים וְלֶב־ רָֽע׃

passages.text: A hateful man disguises himself with his speech, but he lays up deceit in his heart.
passages.sermon: A hateful man speaks to hide his true feelings.\r\nHe uses his words to disguise himself.\r\nHe stores deceit inside his heart.
passages.original: בִּשְׂפָתוֹ יִנָּכֵ֣ר שׂוֹנֵ֑א וּ֝בְקִרְבּ֗וֹ יָשִׁ֥ית מִרְמָֽה׃

passages.text: When he speaks graciously, do not believe him, for seven abominations fill his heart.
passages.sermon:
A hateful man may speak with a gentle voice.
Do not trust him when he speaks kindly.
His heart contains seven abominations.
He hides evil inside himself.
His pleasant words do not show his true nature.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יְחַנֵּ֣ן ק֭וֹלוֹ אַל־ תַּֽאֲמֶן־ בּ֑וֹ כִּ֤י שֶׁ֖בַע תּוֹעֵב֣וֹת בְּלִבּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Though his hatred is concealed by deception, his wickedness will be exposed in the assembly.
passages.sermon:
A hateful man hides his hatred with deception.
He covers his true feelings by pretending.
He does not show his hatred openly.
But his wickedness will become clear in public.
People will see his evil when he stands before others.
His true character will be revealed in the assembly.
passages.original: תִּכַּסֶּ֣ה שִׂ֭נְאָה בְּמַשָּׁא֑וֹן תִּגָּלֶ֖ה רָעָת֣וֹ בְקָהָֽל׃

passages.text: He who digs a pit will fall into it, and he who rolls a stone will have it roll back on him.
passages.sermon:
A person may dig a pit to trap someone else.
That person will fall into the pit himself.
A person may roll a heavy stone to harm another.
That stone will roll back on him.
passages.original: כֹּֽרֶה־ שַּׁ֭חַת בָּ֣הּ יִפֹּ֑ל וְגֹ֥לֵ֥ל אֶ֝בֶן אֵלָ֥יו תָּשֽׁוּב׃

passages.text: A lying tongue hates those it crushes, and a flattering mouth causes ruin.
passages.sermon: A person who lies with their tongue hates the people they harm.\r\nA person who speaks with flattering words causes others to fall into ruin.
passages.original: לְֽשׁוֹן־ שֶׁ֭קֶר יִשְׂנָ֣א דַכָּ֑יו וּפֶ֥ה חָ֝לָ֗ק יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה מִדְחֶֽה׃
